title: Car Sharing Business
desc: Plan a small car-sharing or ride-sharing service: legal checks, insurance, booking, safety, pricing and fairness to drivers and riders.
outcomes: Explain models: peer-to-peer, fleet and carpool.
Set up booking, ID and insurance steps.
Compute cost per hour and per km.
task: Design a small car-sharing service with legal checks, driver and rider vetting, booking flow, insurance, pricing and safety plan.
condition: A computer, a spreadsheet, a practice case, two peers and a mentor. Real vehicles or riders are not used.
standard: Legal and insurance checks are listed with sources; cost per km is correct; vetting and safety steps are written; fairness rules for drivers are included; peers rate Meets or better.
who: Entrepreneurs, community groups, fleet staff, employers with commute schemes.
evidence: legal checklist, booking flow, cost sheet, safety plan, launch plan
modules: There are several ways to share cars.
Peer-to-peer lets owners rent their cars to others.
A fleet owned by an operator is booked by the hour.
Carpooling matches people with seats to riders.
Each model has different legal, insurance and trust needs.
A residential building runs a shared car booked by the hour for members.
Compare three models in a table.
Licences, vehicle checks, tax and permits.
Insurance that covers sharing, not only private use.
Written terms for damage and fines.
Data and privacy rules for location data.
A policy covers hire use only if declared; an undeclared sharing claim is refused.
Check licence and ID; set minimum experience.
Photo of vehicle before and after.
A licence check fails and booking is blocked until the user provides valid documents.
Make the journey smooth and fair.
App or form: choose car, time and deposit.
Digital or key handover; fuel or charge rule.
A checklist records mileage and damage at pickup and return.
Know the real cost per hour and per km.
Fixed: insurance, depreciation, parking. Variable: fuel, wear.
Cost per hour and per km.
Fixed cost 520 INR per day plus 7 INR per km; at 80 km a day, cost per km is 13.5 INR.
Emergency numbers and first aid kit.
A driver reports a flat tyre; roadside help is called and the booking extended.
A rule offers hand controls on request and trains staff.
Pilot with one car and 20 members.
Pilot: 60 per cent utilisation and 1 minor damage.
quiz: Name three models.
Peer-to-peer, fleet, carpool. (Covered in module 1: Models. To pass that module: Pros and cons.)
Why special insurance?
Private cover may not apply. (Covered in module 2: Legal and insurance. To pass that module: Each item has a source.)
Cost per km components?
Fuel, wear. (Covered in module 3: Vetting and ID. To pass that module: Steps clear.)
Why before-and-after photos?
Prove damage. (Covered in module 4: Booking and handover. To pass that module: Flow has 8 steps.)
Name a vetting check.
Licence and ID. (Covered in module 5: Costs and price. To pass that module: Currency shown.)
What is utilisation?
Share of time in use. (Covered in module 6: Safety and incidents. To pass that module: Steps ordered.)
Incident step one?
Make everyone safe. (Covered in module 7: Fairness and community. To pass that module: Rules clear.)
Fairness rule example?
Equal access. (Covered in module 8: Launch plan. To pass that module: Peers follow it.)
What is a pilot?
A small test. (Covered in module 8: Launch plan. To pass that module: Peers follow it.)
Why log incidents?
Review and improve. (Covered in module 8: Launch plan. To pass that module: Peers follow it.)

ladder: Models

L1: learner can name models. Focus module: Models (Understand, 3 h). Three common ways. Key points: Peer-to-peer lending of private cars. A company fleet booked by the hour. Carpool matching shared journeys.

Teach: open with the worked example. A building runs a shared car booked by the hour. Then set the activity: Compare 3 models. Mark against the standard: Pros and cons. Check at this level: Name three models. Model answer: Peer-to-peer, fleet, carpool. Models.
Legal and insurance

L2: learner knows legal basics. Focus module: Legal and insurance (Apply, 5 h). Do not skip this. Key points: Licences, vehicle checks, tax and permits. Insurance that covers sharing, not only private use. Written terms for damage and fines.

Teach: open with the worked example. A policy covers hire use only if declared. Then set the activity: Make a legal checklist. Mark against the standard: Each item has a source. Check at this level: Why special insurance? Model answer: Private cover may not apply. Legal.
Vetting and ID

L3: learner can vet and book. Focus module: Vetting and ID (Apply, 4 h). Know who drives. Key points: Check licence and ID; set minimum experience. Photo of vehicle before and after. Privacy rules for data.

Teach: open with the worked example. A licence check fails and booking is blocked. Then set the activity: Write the vetting steps. Mark against the standard: Steps clear. Check at this level: Cost per km components? Model answer: Fuel, wear. Vet.
Booking and handover

L4: learner can run a day. Focus module: Booking and handover (Apply, 4 h). Smooth and fair. Key points: App or form: choose car, time, deposit. Digital or key handover; fuel or charge rule. Late and cancel rules.

Teach: open with the worked example. A checklist records mileage and damage. Then set the activity: Design the flow. Mark against the standard: Flow has 8 steps. Check at this level: Why before-and-after photos? Model answer: Prove damage. Run.
Costs and price

L5: learner can price. Focus module: Costs and price (Analyse, 5 h). Know the real cost. Key points: Fixed: insurance, depreciation, parking. Variable: fuel, wear. Cost per hour and per km. Utilisation for break-even.

Teach: open with the worked example. Cost 520 INR per day fixed plus 7 INR per km. Then set the activity: Build a cost sheet. Mark against the standard: Currency shown. Check at this level: Name a vetting check. Model answer: Licence and ID. Price.
Fairness and community
L6: learner can lead. Focus module: Fairness and community (Evaluate, 3 h). Treat all fairly. Key points: No discrimination in access. Fair rates and clear fees. Accessibility options.

Teach: open with the worked example. A rule offers hand controls on request. Then set the activity: List fairness rules. Mark against the standard: Rules clear. Check at this level: What is utilisation? Model answer: Share of time in use. Lead.
Launch plan
L7: learner can audit. Focus module: Launch plan (Create, 4 h). Test small. Key points: Pilot with one car and 20 members. Track use, damage and feedback. Improve.

Teach: open with the worked example. Pilot: 60% utilisation, 1 minor damage. Then set the activity: Present the plan. Mark against the standard: Peers follow it. Check at this level: Incident step one? Model answer: Make everyone safe. Peer audit.
